ops.text:
ship --no-push leaves the jj bookmark stale, so a later push is a silent no-op.

`ccx vcs ship --no-push` commits but does not move the branch bookmark: the bookmark
move lives in the push path, so after N `--no-push` ships the jj bookmark still points
at the pre-ship commit while the commits sit above it.

Observed twice on 2026-07-31 during Phase 2 of the gt+jj+worktrees work. After four
`--no-push` ships:

    jj log -r 'main | @-'
    69ae728cd1a0  | fix(vcs): resolve repository identity ...       <- @-
    2b8465744e21 main | fix(vcs): read jj without snapshotting ...  <- bookmark, 4 behind

The failure is silent and deferred. A later `jj git push` pushes the bookmark, which
never moved, and reports `Nothing changed` — so the commits look pushed and are not.
Recovery is `jj bookmark move main --to @-` before pushing.

`--no-push` reads as "do everything except the network call", but it also skips a local
state update the commit arguably owns. Either the bookmark move belongs above the
push/no-push branch, or the report should say the bookmark was left where it was.
